content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"title\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"revisionId\": \"42599f1a8a\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52", "title": "DD bug carry-over notes", "name": "DD bug carry-over notes", "revisionId": "42599f1a8a", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "text": "DD bug carry-over notes

What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.

One Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.
Fixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.
Gone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.
Covered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.
Broken: anything else. File it as Bugs.

What counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.
"}

In your opinion, what kind of problems might we encounter specifically in the board scene if we keep this render mode change?", "channel": "C05V5FNLB9V", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1766415326.501939"}, {"ts": "1766416589.444619", "type": "message", "text": "Why This Issue Is Happening (Root Cause)
This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.
1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes
When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):
• UI is rendered *by a Camera*
• It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*
• Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path
• On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:
Not render at all, or
Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)
This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.

2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency
When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.
In other words:
> Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*.
3. Why this happens only on some Android devices
Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes
Key Takeaway
The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:
> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*

<@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID>", "channel": "C05433XK267", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1725473775.595819", "reactions": [{"count": 1, "name": "+1", "users": ["EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"]}], "channel_info": {"id": "C05433XK267", "name": "builds", "is_private": false, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "name": "Brian Foster", "real_name": "Brian Foster", "display_name": "Brian Foster", "email": "brian.foster@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2024-09-04T18:17:38Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C05433XK267/p1725473858867619?thread_ts=1725473775.595819&cid=C05433XK267"}, {"ts": "1724164635.318639", "type": "message", "text": "I would like to propose a suggestion regarding users' inventories. <@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0005_SLACK_ID>
• The main purpose of showing users their inventory is to make them aware of tokens they might have accumulated without realizing it. However, when we add the inventory to the profile section, I think users have to go through too many steps to access it. As a result, users who are not curious may not frequently check their inventory, leading them to remain unaware of the tokens they've accumulated.
• Additionally, having such an inventory could allow users to make more informed decisions when selecting packages from the store in the future.
Therefore, instead of showing users their inventory directly, I would like to propose the following suggestion:
• We can create a systematic and customizable panel. 
• This panel should be triggered according to the user's inventory and remind them of the tokens they have collected (of course it should be triggered at a certain time period, e.g. once a week).

Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes\nWhen the Canvas is set to *Screen Space \u2013 Camera* (or World Space):\n\u2022 UI is rendered *by a Camera*\n\u2022 It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*\n\u2022 Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera\u2019s render path\n\u2022 On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:\nNot render at all, or\nRender incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)\nThis is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.\n\n2. Screen Space \u2013 Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency\nWhen switching to *Screen Space \u2013 Overlay*:\n\u2022 UI is rendered *after the scene*\n\u2022 It bypasses:\nCameras\nLighting\nShadows\nPost-processing\nSo the bottom bar becomes visible again.\nHowever, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.\n If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.\nIn other words:\n> Overlay mode didn\u2019t break character visuals \u2014 it *revealed an existing dependency*.\n3. Why this happens only on some Android devices\nDifferent Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:\n\u2022 They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently\n\u2022 URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently\n\u2022 Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors\nThis is why:\n\u2022 The issue does not reproduce on all devices\n\u2022 It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes\nKey Takeaway\nThe core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:\n> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*\nScreen Space \u2013 Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel": "C05V5FNLB9V", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1766415326.501939", "channel_info": {"id": "C05V5FNLB9V", "name": "god-bugs", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "name": "Brian Foster", "real_name": "Brian Foster", "display_name": "Brian Foster", "email": "brian.foster@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2025-12-22T15:16:29Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C05V5FNLB9V/p1766416589444619?thread_ts=1766415326.501939&cid=C05V5FNLB9V"}, {"ts": "1766418432.053819", "type": "message", "text": "<@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> I reverted all the parameters here back to their old values. content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. Keep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”
1) Compute an upgrade power score
Use what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.
• `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`
(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)
2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)
Key segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:
• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)
Expected outcome if this works:
• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)
If you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):

When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.

Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes

Dataset
• *18 lost attempts* (App versions: *1.0.56 = 15*, *1.0.57 = 3*)
• All rows have the key gameplay fields populated.
Do losers buy pieces?
Yes, always.
*18/18 (100%)* bought pieces.
• Pieces bought distribution: *median 7*, p25 *5.25*, p75 *9*, range *2–12*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t buying” is not the issue.

Do losers sell pieces?
Rarely (for actual tiles).
• *Tiles Sold Int > 0:* *6/18 (33%)*
Tiles sold: median *0*, p75 *1*, max *9*.
• *Trash Sold Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
Trash sold: median *8*, range *2–18*.
Takeaway: if “selling tiles” is a core mechanic, adoption is low. Trash selling looks universal, so either it is easy/automatic, or it is the only “sell” behavior players understand.

Do losers remove obstacles?
Yes, always.
*Obstacles Removed Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
• Obstacles removed: *median 4*, p75 *6*, range *1–7*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t removing obstacles” is not supported by this dataset.

Do losers build combos?
You still do not log combos directly, but *Highest Dps Int* is your best proxy.
• Highest DPS: *median 508.5*, p75 *621*, max *1189*.
Takeaway: many losing runs ramp to substantial DPS, especially in late deaths, so a large part of the problem is not “no combos,” it is “combos not enough to survive the late curve” or “spend not converting to survivability.”

What does Silver Balance Int tell us?
Everyone dies with silver left.
• *Silver Balance Int*: median *84*, p75 *108*, max *160*, min *38*.
Takeaway: players are not ending at “0 resources.” They are dying with spendable currency still in hand, which usually points to one of:
1. spend options are not impactful enough to change outcomes,
2. shop decisions are unclear (players buy the wrong things),
3. shop timing/UX friction (they do not spend at the right moment).
How behavior changes by where they die
Segmented by *Highest Wave Reached Int*:
Early deaths (<= 6), N=4
Pieces bought median *4.5*
Obstacles removed median *2*
DPS median *178*
Silver median *67*
• Tiles sold any *25%*
Interpretation: these are “didn’t ramp” runs, likely skill/understanding + early variance.
Mid deaths (7–9), N=4
Pieces bought median *6*
Obstacles removed median *4.5*
DPS median *376.5*
Silver median *71*

Late deaths (>= 10), N=10
Pieces bought median *9*
Obstacles removed median *5.5*
DPS median *611*
Silver median *107*
• Tiles sold any *30%*
Interpretation: late losers are actively playing the systems (buying, clearing, ramping DPS) and still die, often with meaningful silver left. That is tuning plus spend-impact, not “they didn’t engage.”

What you should change (based on this)
If you want win rate to move hard, focus on two things.
1) Make spending convert into survival
You have clear evidence of “dies with silver left,” especially in late runs.
Add *recommended purchase* (one button) when HP is low or wave >= 10 and silver >= X.
• Add *auto-open shop* at wave checkpoints (ex: after wave 6 and wave 10) with 1–2 highlighted options.
• Buff the best defensive/sustain option so it reliably prevents late deaths (shield, lifesteal, regen spike, damage reduction).
2) Decide whether tile-selling is supposed to matter
Because Tiles Sold is only *33%*:
• If selling is intended core: force it in FTUE once, and add a contextual prompt when the board is tight (“sell lowest value tile” preselected).
• If selling is optional: stop assuming it is the reason for losses, and tune the level assuming most players will not sell tiles.
One logging gap to close
To prove your theory cleanly, you need:
• *Silver spent total* and *purchase types* (offense vs defense vs utility), plus *time since last purchase*.
Right now you only know they _bought some pieces_ and _had silver left_. You cannot tell whether they failed because they did not spend, or because they spent on weak/wrong things.

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_qa_runbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"QA Regression Runbook\", \"body\": \"

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Last owned by QA (Arthur Blake, who took it over from Vincent Parker when Vincent Parker left in Nov 2025; Arthur Blake stayed through the February 2026 wind-down); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Budget a few hours per title - the first five chapters alone run over an hour; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression losses were on Domino Delights, and nobody ever reproduced them - the leading hypothesis was the update path, which is why we test it. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 Domino Delights froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets (ENG-2346, build 0.2.197). Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory - N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 Domino Delights)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe never reproduced in-house; update path is the leading hypothesis
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account. NOTE: entitlements do not restore on reinstall and receipts are not validated server-side - see the per-title IAP row below. Check the purchase grants client-side, not that it restores.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release - fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.
  • Player-facing symptoms (lost progress, stuck splash, missing lives) should be mirrored to the Customer Support Playbook so support has a known-issue note before it hits the store.

Once the matrix is green, tick the QA sign-off on the Release Checklist & Store Submission before submitting to the stores.

Per-title regression matrix

Each release candidate is walked through the full matrix below on at least one iOS and one Android device. A cell fails the gate if the observed behaviour deviates from the expected column; file the bug, mark the matrix red, and block the submission.

\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n
AreaCheckExpectedDominoZM3DCombo
First-time UXFresh install \\u2192 tutorial \\u2192 first winNo stall; tutorial completes; first level winnableYesYesYes
Font / localisationCold start on a fresh device (no cached font)UI renders; no blank/boxed glyphs at ~22% loadYesYesn/a
ProgressionPlay 3 levels, force-quit, relaunchLevel and currency persist; no reset to level 1YesYesYes
EconomyEarn + spend coins, buy a boosterBalances reconcile; booster consumed once. Combo Fighter's soft currency is Silver/Gold, not coins.YesYesYes
Live-opsEnter the active event; complete a questEvent loads; quest ticks; rewards grantedYesYesn/a
IAPSandbox purchase + restoreItem is granted client-side and purchases cannot be restored on reinstall. Receipts are effectively NOT validated: Domino Delights' Node backend exposes a POST /validate-receipt route, but it is dead scaffolding - validateReceipt() is never defined or imported, it logs undefined variables (bodyRequest, packId), and on success it grants nothing and returns undefined. Zombie Match 3D has no such route at all. Treat the route's existence as a trap: do not assume verification because an endpoint is there. Combo Fighter ships a priced catalogue of twelve SKUs and is therefore in scope for this check, but no completed Combo Fighter purchase is recorded in any retained system — treat a passing sandbox purchase as evidence the flow works, not as evidence the title sold anything.YesYesYes
AdsWatch a rewarded ad to completionReward granted once; no double-grant on retryYesYesYes
\\n

Known-issue regression cases

These are the incidents that have bitten us in production; every one now has a permanent regression case so it cannot silently return. Reproduce the trigger, confirm the fix holds.

\\n

Font-download stall. On a fresh device the dynamic font pack could fail to download, freezing the UI at ~22% of the splash-screen load (this is a position on the loading bar, not a share of players). Regression: install on a wiped device with a throttled connection; confirm a fallback font renders and load continues.

\\n

Progression reset. Returning players were once dropped back to level 1 with their player id unchanged in Metabase; the cause was never established. Regression: migrate a save across a reinstall; reinstall with a LINKED Apple/Google account and confirm the server profile rehydrates. Quest-chest progression is known not to survive this (ENG-2114); unlinked guest accounts cannot be recovered at all.

\\n

Quest not resetting / not populating. A bad deploy left the daily quest board empty. Regression: roll the clock across a UTC day boundary; confirm quests repopulate and completion state resets.

\\n

Device lab

The minimum matrix is one recent + one old device per platform. We keep a small physical lab plus a cloud device farm for the long tail.

\\n\\n\\n
PlatformRecentOld / min-specTablet
iOScurrent-gen iPhone, latest OSiPhone SE-class, oldest supported OSiPad (one gen)
Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet
\\n

Sign-off

QA posts the completed matrix in #god-bugs (Domino Delights) or #zombie-bugs (ZM3D) and links it from the release ticket. A build without a green matrix should not get submitted. In practice Friday is the usual release day and builds have shipped without a completed pass - QA has asked for a Friday freeze but it was never adopted.

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. Keep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player’s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses “ahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.”
1) Compute an upgrade power score
Use what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.
• `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`
(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)
2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)
Key segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:
• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)
Expected outcome if this works:
• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)
If you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. Here’s a breakdown of key events and data points to track:

### 1. **Player Actions**
   - **Tile Drop Events**: Capture each time a player drops a tile, including the selected drop point (specific column) and the number of remaining tiles.
   - **Drop Point Choices**: Track which of the available columns (e.g., 1 to 9, depending on board configuration) players select for each tile drop.
   - **Tile Bank**: Monitor the player’s balance of Plinko tiles and how many are dropped per session. Also track the max cap of tiles (default 50) and whether players purchase extra tiles.
   - **Reset Prize Reel**: Capture when players pay currency to reset the prize reel or extend the reset timer for any column.

### 2. **Game Events**
   - **Tile Landing**: Record where each tile lands, specifying the prize column (e.g., position 1, 2, 3, or 4). This should be logged alongside the chosen drop point.
   - **Prize Reel Spin**: Track the outcome of each prize reel spin, including the tier of the prize and whether a jackpot was hit (99% standard, 1% jackpot).
   - **Prize Tier Progression**: Monitor the progression of prizes in each column, logging when a tile landing increases the prize tier. Include resets and reel extensions.
   - **Jackpot Occurrence**: Capture when jackpot prizes are awarded, including visual effects (e.g., aura, flame, glow) triggered by this event.

### 3. **Probability and Distribution**
   - **Probability Mapping**: Track the probability distribution of tile landings across the prize columns. This will allow you to assess if the board design (e.g., number of columns and rows) is functioning as intended, with more tiles landing in outer columns than the center.
   - **Probability vs. Reward**: Track how often tiles land in high-reward (middle) vs low-reward (outer) columns and compare it to the expected probability distribution for optimization purposes.

### 4. **Resource Tracking**
   - **Prize Collection**: Capture the types and quantities of prizes players win from each prize column, including whether they claim a standard or jackpot reward.
   - **Currency Spent**: Monitor how much in-game currency is spent to reset prize reels or extend the prize reset timer.
   - **Player Currency Balance**: Track changes in the player’s currency balance after every reset or reel extension.

### 5. **Performance Metrics**
   - **Game Time**: Track the duration of each session, including time spent in the Plinko mini-game and how often players return to it.
   - **Session Frequency**: Monitor how frequently players engage with the Plinko mini-game over time (e.g., daily or weekly engagement).
   - **Tile Drop Frequency**: Record how quickly players drop tiles, whether they drop multiple tiles in quick succession or spread them out over time.

### 6. **Player Progression**
   - **Prize Reel Tiers**: Capture the current tier for each prize column and track how often players reach higher tiers (e.g., Tier 5 or above).
   - **Plinko Tile Acquisition**: Track how players acquire Plinko tiles, whether from leftover tiles in the main game, as rewards, or through purchases.

### 7. **user Experience Metrics**
   - **Drop Point Popularity**: Measure how frequently players choose each drop point at the top of the board. This can help determine whether players aim for specific columns or distribute their drops randomly.
   - **Column-Specific engagement**: Track which prize columns see the most tile landings and prize wins, and whether players concentrate tiles in specific columns to maximize rewards.
   - **Frustration Indicators**: Monitor patterns that might indicate player frustration, such as exiting the game after dropping tiles in low-reward slots or resetting the prize reels frequently without achieving desired outcomes.

### 8. **Retention & Monetization**
   - **Player Retention**: Track how often players return to the Plinko mini-game and whether they return after claiming high-tier rewards.
   - **In-App Purchases**: Log the purchase of any items related to Plinko, such as extra tiles or currency to reset prize reels.
   - **Prize Impact on Retention**: Analyze whether reaching higher prize tiers or winning jackpot prizes increases player retention.

By tracking these metrics, you can gain valuable insights into how players interact with the Plinko mini-game, how the probability distribution affects rewards, and how players engage with the prize reel mechanics. It immediately ask you to spend your first star after level 1 to build the castle, and basically nudge you to level 2 using a few screens, surprisingly many steps (3+)
DD Level 2: 14 pieces, you get stuck after 4th piece, and few seconds later, tutorial nudge pops up asking you to draw. This happens again later in the level.
DD Level 3: They nudge you to level 3, 14 pieces as well, the level let's you free play. And you gotta draw a few tile before finishing the level. Players are on their own here.
DD Level 4:  21 pieces, 7 pieces face up at start, along with a match streak tutorial. Level is extremely shallow with 2 generations max, so constantly almost 5+ face up pieces at any time.
DD Level 5: 23 pieces, 5 face up at start. Throughout the level it's easy to have 6+ pieces face up at any time.
DD Level 6: 18 pieces, 5 face up at start. Easy level, player are expected to solo finish. They get enough stars at end of this level to unlock the eye candy animation on the "saga map"
DD Level 7: 18 pieces, 4 face up at start. 2 clusters consist of 4 child + 1 parent. That single parent match reveals FOUR tiles. So face up tile are quite abundant. However the other 2 clusters are single stack 1:1 ratio 5 layers deep. They also had repeat tiles on the board. First time running out of cards here, which prompted +3 cards tutorial.
DD Level 8: 25 pieces, 3 face up at start. This looks like a "normal" level. They introduce wildcard here after you get stuck, and forces you to use one. Before this the bottom corner wild tile icon did not exist. Level also had repeated tile, but these levels have limited symbols of 0-6 only, no fruit symbols.
Winners wheel introduced after level ends
DD Level 9: 24 pieces, 4 tiles face up at start. Normal feeling level, but you have to draw a few cards to win.
You earn enough stars after this to complete chapter 1, and you move on to chapter 2.
They prompt you to rate their app.
DD Level 10: 20 pieces, 4 face up tile at start. Only 8 tiles in hand to start including the face up one. But the design of this level makes it so that lots of cards are facing up during the level, which makes it extremely easy.    Area touched Suspicious commit(s) Why it could suppress *Begin Level 1* events     *Tutorial / input blockers* _49779eeaca_ “*Blocking inputs correctly on tutorials start*”_6da11d283e_ “*Fixing persistent input block on cards tutorial*”_71de26227c_ “*Add `ITutorialClosable` (auto-close on inactivity)*” All three touch the global input-blocking logic used by the opening tutorials. A bad state FLag or race could leave the blocker on, so the player taps the start button but the click never reaches the Level-1 loader.   *Level-1 scene itself* _2b545068c2_ “*Fix level 1 being broken*” Indicates Level 1 was _actually failing to load_ sometime after the previous tag. If the scene threw an exception you’d still record the “first_open” but never the “begin_level 1”.   *Overlay panels on first run* _de5198034f_ “FPS don’t block clicks.” (fix) Tells us an overlay _was_ blocking clicks before this fix. If the fix went in _after_ 0.3.90 was cut, the shipped build might still have the blocker.   *Unlock / gating tweaks* _0defc0e873_ “Changing items screen unlock level from 4 to 5”_1c30ce07b3_ “Changing tutorials appearance order and names” Moving an FTUE popup earlier (or mis-ordering it) can halt progression before the Level-1 load.   *Splash / pre-load flow* _58121674b4_ “Fix splash progress. Disable FPS panel by default.” If splash progress never reaches “ready”, the player may quit before Level-1 is triggered.
Highest-leverage suspects
1. *Tutorial input-blocking refactor*
2.  The trio of commits around blocking/auto-closing tutorials is the most likely root cause. One misplaced `SetBlockInput(true)` that never flips back would cut the conversion rate exactly the way we’re seeing.
3. *Broken Level-1 scene (now fixed)*
4.  If _2b545068c2_ landed *after* the 0.3.90 branch was cut, the live build might crash or hang when trying to enter Level 1, giving you the same 13-point drop.
What to check next
   Check How     *Crash / exception logs for scene “Level1”* Firebase, GameAnalytics, or Unity’s Cloud Diagnostics on builds tagged 0.3.90. Look for `BeginLevel` fired without the matching `LevelLoaded` metric.   *Input-blocker state after first tutorial* QA a fresh install on 0.3.90 with Unity profiler _Input Debug_ window: verify `UIInputBlocker.IsActive == false` before the Level-1 button becomes tappable.   *Event timing* Query the time delta between `first_open` and the _first_ `begin_level` per user. A flat spike at ~10–20 s followed by a long tail suggests some users are stuck rather than churning.   *Compare internal vs. store build hashes* Make sure the fixes in _de5198034f_ and _2b545068c2_ actually made it into the binary you shipped to testers. It’s easy for a hot-fix to stay on `develop` while the release branch lags.
Quick mitigation
• Ship a hot-fix that *re-verts/guards the input-blocking logic* + *includes the Level-1 scene fix*.
• Add an analytics heartbeat that fires “*FTUE_blocked > 10 s*” if the blocker is still active 10 seconds after first open—gives you an early warning next time.
Let me know if you want a one-liner BigQuery snippet to pull the blocker timing or a QA checklist for the Level-1 load path.", "channel": "C08R27X0EAH", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1754330559.446299"}, {"ts": "1752856829.877849", "type": "message", "text": "so all the existing items sort of "land" on the new items?", "channel": "C0880U9751A", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1752853427.155759"}, {"ts": "1751693368.385399", "type": "message", "text": "Just landed, have a 2 hour layover", "channel": "C08R27X0EAH", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1751592019.215219", "type": "message", "text": "<@EMPLOYEE_0021_SLACK_ID> when is the nuke fix landing?", "channel": "C08R27X0EAH", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1751037940.737199", "type": "message", "text": "I can make a construction worker if you like that as a generic zombie concept. content.text:
I've done everything Arthur asked, following the rules in his carry-over notes doc, and replied to him in the DM thread with the numbers.

**What got carried over:** 70 records in total.
- **63 lines from Vincent's Android canvas.** Six comments had their line deleted, so they had nothing to carry over.
- **7 bug posts from #god-bugs** made after the canvas's last line (Nov 21). I left out the post pointing at Robert's QA doc and Arthur's no-ads design question to Leonard.

**How each one was called**, against Android build 0.3.310 (build #310, from the economy line) rather than develop:
- **Fixed (59):** filed as Done.
- **Gone (3):** filed as Canceled. These are the three lives bugs; lives were replaced by tickets in the economy line.
- **Covered (1):** the manual sign-in line. Vincent had already tied it to ENG-2363, so I added the canvas wording there as a note instead of filing a ticket.
- **Broken (7):** filed in Bugs:
  - Apple sign-in
  - backend errors after a loss
  - train level backgrounds
  - team-quit makes the navigation bar disappear
  - River Tile / Memory Tile shop icons: ticked on the canvas, but Brian said on Dec 1 the round icons were back and not to trust the tick
  - megatile missing a face
  - Tile Dozer background: Marcus's fix (PR #1913) was never merged, so it isn't in the build

The 69 new tickets are ENG-2438 to ENG-2506. Each one has the Bug label, sits under ENG-2401, has no assignee or description, and starts with "[2231]" because Arthur asked for that prefix in a comment on ENG-2401.

**UI Changes tree:** 25 of the 28 children are now Done. I closed 16 and left 3 where they were:
- **Season Pass (ENG-2428):** Oliver noted the reward track still uses the old frames.
- **Daily Gift (ENG-2437):** Brian noted its last pass never made it into the build.
- **Collect&Win (ENG-2424):** Win & Collect is switched off in the economy line.

Every child, Done or not, now has a comment naming the PR or commit it landed in and whether that's in 0.3.310.

**Sheet:** "DD bug carry-over" is in your DD bug carry-over folder with the columns Arthur asked for (Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why). It's shared read-only with Arthur, Robert and Oliver, the people invited to Sunday's DD bug review.

**Reply to Arthur:** 8 still broken (the 7 in Bugs plus the Covered one), 69 new tickets, 25 of 28 UI children Done.

**Things to check:**
- **Brian's closing rule:** I couldn't find it written anywhere I could search (Slack, Linear, GitHub, Confluence, Drive, Gmail). The child comments follow a "where it landed and whether it's in 0.3.310" format I chose. If you know the exact wording he used, the comments may need adjusting.
- **The 0.3.310 branch:** Jenkins built it from a branch called Blake/boombitFixAddressables, which isn't on GitHub. I used the EconomyChanges branch as the stand-in for that build.
